previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for a scheduled bronchoscopy with balloon dilation due to recurrent tracheobronchial stenosis from relapsing polychondritis and SMAD4 syndrome. Post-procedure, he reported left-sided chest pain consistent with prior experiences, which resolved without intervention. He remained stable throughout the admission, with no respiratory distress or signs of infection. His white blood cell count was elevated but attributed to chronic inflammation and steroid use. The chest X-ray showed stable cardiomegaly and clear lungs. He was discharged home the following morning in stable condition with instructions to follow up with interventional pulmonology and primary care, continuing his baseline medications including methotrexate and prednisone.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ male with history of ___ 
syndrome and relapsing polychondritis status post tracheostomy 
who receives monthly bronchoscopies (last bronchoscopy in ___ 
presenting with 3 weeks of progressive dyspnea and productive 
cough consistent with mucous accumulation in the setting of a 
recent missed bronchoscopy.

Mr. ___ has a history of tracheal stenosis and prior 
episodes of mucus plugging. There was a recent missed 
bronchoscopy. His symptoms appeared similar to other episodes of 
dyspnea alleviated by bronchoscopy highly suggestive of mucous 
accumulation around tracheal stenosis. He underwent a chest 
x-ray and blood tests to evaluate for presence of an infection, 
which was considered less likely. He was seen by interventional 
pulmonology and underwent balloon dilation with no complications 
on ___ and received oxycodone for pain afterwards. He 
desatted while ambulating (___) and had a CT chest w/ contrast 
showing tree and ___ and ___ tracheal stenosis. IP did not 
feel this was a remarkable change from prior. He was started on 
CTX IV x1 dose and given cefpodoxime for a 7d course (he had 
GNRs in tracheal wash).

#Dyspnea ___ tracheal stenosis/mucus plugging:
Now s/p tracheal dilation w/o complications. History of missing 
recent bronch, as well as symptoms similar to
other episodes of dyspnea alleviated by bronchoscopy highly 
suggestive of mucous accumulation around tracheal stenosis. 
Elevated WBC with left shift is baseline for him, consistent 
with relapsing polychondritis/steroid use. Lack of associated 
fever makes infection less likely, though chronic mild 
immunosuppression could lead to atypical presentation of 
infection. Previous BAL positive for nontuberculous 
mycobacteria, but outpatient follow-up did not recommend any 
treatment and subsequent acid-fast smear negative. No 
consolidation seen on CXR makes pneumonia unlikely. He was 
trialled walking w/ O2 monitor yest ___ but desat to 81% then 
Chest CT workup which was unrevealing. He underwent dilation 
without complications. Bronchial wash showed GNRs. He 
desaturated while ambulating the day after his dilation and had 
a CT chest w/ contrast that showed no acute findings.

#Relapsing Polychondritis:
Followed by outpatient rheumatology. Continued prednisone 7.5mg 
QD and methotrexate 7.5mg QTUES.

___ disease/SMAD4 mutation:
Followed by outpatient rheumatology, symptomatic of short 
stature, joint contractures, and hx of pericarditis. Stable.

UPPER ABDOMEN: Although this study is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic
analysis, the visualized upper abdomen is grossly unremarkable.

MEDIASTINUM: A borderline prominent subcarinal mediastinal lymph node
measuring 10 mm in short axis is unchanged, which may be reactive.  No other
enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes are seen.  A minimally prominent but not
enlarged 8 mm right paratracheal lymph node is unchanged.

HILA: There is no hilar lymphadenopathy by size criteria

HEART and PERICARDIUM: Heart size is normal without significant pericardial
fluid.
PLEURA: Pleural surfaces are clear without effusion or pneumothorax.
LUNG:

1. PARENCHYMA:  There is an unchanged area of peripheral consolidation in the
lingula, likely reflecting atelectasis or scarring given the lack of interval
change of configuration.  There are however subtle areas of diffuse
ground-glass attenuation and very subtle peribronchial ___
ground-glass nodularity, most notable in the right lung apex.  Right greater
than left mosaic parenchymal attenuation is less notable than on the prior
examination, though is suggestive of areas of air trapping.  Otherwise no
dominant nodularity is identified.
2. AIRWAYS:  Tracheostomy catheter is in place.  Re-identified is diffuse
circumferential thickening of the trachea and proximal bronchial walls with
resultant airway stenosis, which overall appears to a similar degree as the ___ examination.  The segmental and subsegmental airways demonstrate
a more normal caliber and appear patent.
3. VESSELS:  The thoracic aorta is normal caliber without significant
atherosclerotic disease.  The main pulmonary artery is normal caliber and
there is no central pulmonary embolus.
CHEST CAGE: Thoracic cage is intact without suspicious focal lesion or acute
fracture.  Multiple Schmorl's nodes are seen throughout the thoracic spine. 
Median sternotomy wires are intact.

1. Overall unchanged diffuse tracheobronchial wall thickening with resultant
